column6: The cover names the repository URL and the full hash of the named commit, and the PDF carries the six living docs other than the decision records (docs/requirements.md, docs/design.md, docs/risks.md, README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, and the AI context file), rendered and matching that commit. Where an NDA walkthrough stands in, a document the partner keeps out of the PDF does not count against the team, and a sanitized PDF matches the commit if it differs only in what was redacted.
column9: One of the six living docs other than the decision records is missing from the PDF, not rendered, or does not match the named commit. Where an NDA walkthrough stands in, a document the partner keeps out of the PDF does not count against the team, and a sanitized PDF matches the commit if it differs only in what was redacted.
column12: The cover lacks the repository URL or the full commit hash, or two or more of the six living docs other than the decision records are missing from the PDF, not rendered, or do not match the named commit. Where an NDA walkthrough stands in, a document the partner keeps out of the PDF does not count against the team, and a sanitized PDF matches the commit if it differs only in what was redacted.

column6: Every milestone item for this checkpoint is met: CI ran on the named commit and passed (for a FOSS project, upstream's CI on your pull request, or the build-and-test command your fork documents until your first one; with no product code yet, on a scaffold with at least one test that fails when the scaffold breaks), linked on the cover; every item in the current sprint on the board linked on the cover has an owner and a status; docs/design.md records where the walking skeleton will run, who owns the account or infrastructure, and who agreed it, with, for a FOSS project, who upstream reviews the first pull request, or, for a research project, which sample data the pipeline may use and, if the real-data run will happen on a single workstation, who outside the team will run it there; or docs/design.md records that there will be no deployment, why, and what ships instead; docs/risks.md names any approval the target needs, who is asking for it, and when they asked; and, for a team starting in an existing codebase, the inherited-codebase audit is in the PDF and covers each of its items (what runs and how, and what does not; the state of the tests and the CI; the dependencies and their age; the open risks and the known debt; the predecessor team's handoff document and the forward-looking section of their project retrospective, if there is one; the upstream project's contribution rules, if there are any; what the team will change first). Where an NDA walkthrough stands in, a document the partner keeps out of the PDF does not count against the team, and a sanitized PDF matches the commit if it differs only in what was redacted.
column9: One milestone item is unmet or only demonstrable with help, and the cover names it with an owner and a date to close it (e.g., the production target is recorded but nobody has agreed it yet, the approval it needs is named in docs/risks.md but nobody has asked for it yet, or the audit leaves out an item it asks for).
column12: Two or more milestone items are unmet, or one is unmet and the cover names no owner and date to close it.

column2: Docs current and consistent with the code [SO2]
column6: The five documents this criterion covers (docs/requirements.md, docs/design.md, README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, and the AI context file, such as AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md) exist, are in the PDF, rendered and matching the named commit, and pass the spot-check: docs/design.md describes the system that exists, and docs/requirements.md gives an acceptance criterion wherever a requirement's behavior is not obvious (for a finished functional requirement, the name of its test in CI will do), and lists under Constraints the limits the team did not choose. Whether the README.md quickstart runs is scored under Build health. Where an NDA walkthrough stands in, a document the partner keeps out of the PDF does not count against the team, and a sanitized PDF matches the commit if it differs only in what was redacted.
column9: One of the five is absent from the repository or has drifted from the code, one is missing from the PDF, not rendered, or does not match the named commit, or some are missing sections. Where an NDA walkthrough stands in, a document the partner keeps out of the PDF does not count against the team, and a sanitized PDF matches the commit if it differs only in what was redacted.
column12: Two or more of the five are absent from the repository or have drifted from the code, or two or more are missing from the PDF, not rendered, or do not match the named commit. Where an NDA walkthrough stands in, a document the partner keeps out of the PDF does not count against the team, and a sanitized PDF matches the commit if it differs only in what was redacted.

column6: Decisions are recorded in docs/rfcs/ or docs/adr/: RFC drafts committed with status Proposed and naming the options they weigh, or with their outcome and the options rejected and why if the team has decided since, and an ADR naming the options rejected and why for any decision already taken; docs/risks.md is the single risk register, with risks, each ranked and with an owner; docs/risks.md is in the PDF, rendered and matching the named commit, the cover links docs/rfcs/ or docs/adr/ at that commit, and no duplicate register exists elsewhere. Where an NDA walkthrough stands in, a document the partner keeps out of the PDF does not count against the team, and a sanitized PDF matches the commit if it differs only in what was redacted.
column9: Decisions and risks are tracked but incompletely: some decisions unrecorded or recorded without the options weighed or rejected, ranking or owners missing on some risks, a second register exists, docs/risks.md is missing from the PDF, not rendered, or does not match the named commit, or the cover does not link docs/rfcs/ or docs/adr/. Where an NDA walkthrough stands in, a document the partner keeps out of the PDF does not count against the team, and a sanitized PDF matches the commit if it differs only in what was redacted.
column12: No recorded decisions, no docs/risks.md or an empty one, or a register with neither ranking nor owners, or docs/risks.md is missing from the PDF, not rendered, or does not match the named commit, and the cover does not link docs/rfcs/ or docs/adr/ either. Where an NDA walkthrough stands in, a document the partner keeps out of the PDF does not count against the team, and a sanitized PDF matches the commit if it differs only in what was redacted.

column6: CI runs the tests on every pull request (for a FOSS project, upstream's CI on your pull requests, or the build-and-test command your fork documents until your first one); at least one test would fail if the feature it covers broke; a grader can follow the quickstart cold. The checks match how much the team delegates: review gates on the changes that are expensive to undo (schema, authentication, deployment, migrations), and docs/risks.md or README.md names where changes will be exercised before they reach users (a staging or preview environment, a store beta track, a dedicated test device, a run on sample data) and how a bad change will be undone, each with the date it lands.
column9: CI and tests exist, but the quickstart runs only with a step README.md does not give, or the checks have visible gaps relative to how the team works: no gate on a hard-to-undo path, or no plan for where changes will be exercised before they reach users or how a bad change will be undone.
column12: CI or tests are absent, no test would fail if the feature it covers broke, the quickstart does not work, or nothing gates a hard-to-undo change and there is no plan to undo one.

column2: Contribution traceability and version control hygiene [SO5]
column6: Each student's work is attributable over the period: code through reviewed PRs under real accounts, other work where CONTRIBUTING.md says it lives, and the Contribution lines in the sprint notes match that record. The history is one a maintainer could inherit: nothing lands on the default branch outside a pull request; no live secrets, build artifacts, or dependency directories are in the history (if a secret leaked, it was revoked or rotated, and the commit that removed it says so); commit messages say what changed and why, with noisy branches squashed on merge; nobody force-pushes the default branch; and large binaries are out of Git or in Git LFS.
column9: Most students' work is traceable, but some of it cannot be attributed, or the history misses any of those items (direct commits to the default branch, committed build artifacts or dependency directories, commit messages that do not say what changed and why, noisy branches merged unsquashed, a force-push to the default branch, large binaries outside Git LFS).
column12: Contribution cannot be traced to individuals over the period, or a secret was committed and never rotated.
